questions.question: Which assumptions describe the dynamic lot-size model?
options: Known demands varying by period, no shortages, no lead time
A constant demand rate, no shortages, instant delivery
Uncertain demand in one period, ordered before it is seen
Known varying demands, with shortages backordered

questions.question: In the dynamic lot-size model ($y_i$ is the order in period $i$, $D_i$ the known demand, $x_i$ the starting stock, $K_i$ the setup cost, $c_i(y_i)$ the variable ordering cost and $h_i$ the holding cost per unit carried from period $i$ to $i+1$), why is the stock carried forward required to satisfy $x_{i+1}\ge0$?
options: It keeps holding costs from becoming negative.
It forces stock to be left over at the end of the horizon.
Negative stock would be unmet demand, a shortage.
It makes every period's order at least its demand.

questions.question: In a dynamic lot-size plan with starting stock $x_1=0$, demands $D=(3,2,4)$ and orders $y=(5,0,4)$ for periods 1 to 3, using $x_{i+1}=x_i+y_i-D_i$, what are the stocks $x_2$, $x_3$, $x_4$ carried into the next periods?

A 3-period dynamic lot-size plan has $x_1=0$, demands $D=(3,2,4)$ and orders $y=(5,0,4)$, setup cost $K_i=10$ in every period, variable cost $c_i(y_i)=2y_i$ and holding cost $h_i=1$ per unit carried to the next period. What is the total cost $\sum_i[C_i(y_i)+h_ix_{i+1}]$?
For a dynamic lot-size model with $x_1=0$ and demands $D=(3,2,4)$, a planner proposes orders $y=(2,4,3)$. Using $x_{i+1}=x_i+y_i-D_i\ge0$, why is this plan infeasible?
options: Period 3 orders only 3 units for its demand of 4.
Stock after period 3 would be $-1$, a shortage.
Stock after period 2 would be $3$, too much.
Stock after period 1 would be $-1$, a shortage.

questions.question: A dynamic lot-size model has starting stock $x_1=3$, demands $D=(4,6,5)$ and terminal stock $x_4=0$. What must the total of the orders $y_1+y_2+y_3$ be?
In a dynamic lot-size model, period 2 has setup cost $K_2=50$ and variable ordering cost $c_2(y_2)=3y_2$. What is the ordering cost $C_2(y_2)$ for an order of $y_2=4$ units?

In a dynamic lot-size model with the same unit price in every period, a planner considers adding period 3's demand $D_3$ to the order of period 2 instead of ordering in period 3. Period 3 has setup cost $K_3$, and carrying a unit from period 2 to 3 costs $h_2$. When does this lower the total cost?
options: When $h_2D_3<K_3$
When $K_3<h_2D_3$
When $D_3<D_2$
When $h_2<K_3$

questions.question: In a dynamic lot-size model with linear variable cost $c_i(y_i)=cy_i$, the same unit price $c$ in every period, given $x_1$ and terminal stock $x_{n+1}=0$, does the variable cost affect which plan is cheapest?
options: Yes; plans with larger orders pay more variable cost.
No; all feasible plans order the same total amount.
Yes; it decides how many periods have a setup.
No; variable cost is never part of the objective.

questions.question: In a dynamic lot-size model with positive holding costs and nonnegative ordering costs, why is it reasonable to require terminal stock $x_{n+1}=0$?
options: Leftover final stock adds cost but meets no demand.
It guarantees that no setup is needed in the last period.
Otherwise the balance equations would have no solution.
It forces every period to end with zero stock.

questions.question: A 3-period dynamic lot-size model has $x_1=0$, demands $D=(2,1,3)$, setup cost 10 in every period, the same unit price every period and holding cost 1 per unit carried to the next period. Which of these plans has the lowest setup plus holding cost?
options: Order 3 in period 1 and 3 in period 3, at cost 21
Order all 6 units in period 1, at cost 17
Order each period's own demand, at cost 30
Order 2 in period 1 and 4 in period 2, at cost 23

questions.question: In a dynamic lot-size model with holding costs $h_1=2$ and $h_2=1$ per unit carried to the next period, 3 units ordered in period 1 are kept until they meet demand in period 3, and nothing else is carried. What holding cost do these units cause?

In the dynamic lot-size model, the total cost is $\sum_i[C_i(y_i)+h_ix_{i+1}]$ with $C_i(y_i)=0$ for $y_i=0$ and $K_i+cy_i$ for $y_i>0$, where $K_i>0$. Why is this not a linear program in the variables $y_i$ and $x_i$ alone?
options: The balance $x_{i+1}=x_i+y_i-D_i$ is not linear.
The jump of $C_i$ by $K_i$ at $y_i>0$ is not linear.
The constraint $x_{i+1}\ge0$ cannot appear in an LP.
Holding cost $h_ix_{i+1}$ is quadratic in the stock.

questions.question: In a dynamic lot-size model, every setup cost is $K_i=0$, the unit price is the same in every period and every holding cost $h_i$ is positive. Which plan has the lowest cost?
options: Order exactly each period's demand in that period.
Order all demand in period 1, to save setups.
Any plan, since all costs are then the same.
Order in alternate periods, to balance setup and holding.

questions.question: A 2-period dynamic lot-size model has no setup costs, demands $D=(3,4)$, unit prices $c_1=5$ and $c_2=8$ (so $c_i(y_i)=c_iy_i$), holding cost $h_1=2$ per unit carried into period 2, $x_1=0$ and $x_3=0$. What is the lowest total cost?

A 3-period dynamic lot-size model has $x_1=0$, demands $D=(2,2,2)$, setup costs $K=(30,3,30)$, the same unit price every period, holding cost 1 per unit carried to the next period and $x_4=0$. What is the lowest setup plus holding cost over all feasible plans?
